name: Networking Fabric
blurb: InfiniBand, Ethernet, and interconnect topology for training clusters.

items.name: Arista AI networking
items.note: Ethernet switching platforms for AI back-end networks at hyperscalers

items.name: Quantum InfiniBand
items.note: The dominant training-cluster interconnect; the Mellanox acquisition that became NVIDIA's moat beyond the GPU

items.name: NVLink / NVSwitch
items.note: The intra-node and rack-scale GPU fabric; NVL72 puts 72 GPUs in one NVLink domain

items.name: Tomahawk switch silicon
items.note: Merchant Ethernet switch chips (51.2T Tomahawk 5 onward) powering AI clusters that choose Ethernet over InfiniBand

reading.body:
Five entries make up this collection, split between NVIDIA's InfiniBand and NVLink technologies and the Ethernet-based alternatives being built to compete with them, Arista's switching platforms and Broadcom's Tomahawk silicon.

NVIDIA's Quantum InfiniBand is described as the dominant training-cluster interconnect and the product of its Mellanox acquisition, which the data calls NVIDIA's moat beyond the GPU itself, while its NVLink and NVSwitch technology is described separately as the intra-node and rack-scale fabric, with the NVL72 configuration putting 72 GPUs inside one NVLink domain, the same rack system named elsewhere in this site's power and cooling data as the reason 120-kilowatt racks ended air cooling's run. Broadcom's Tomahawk 5 switch silicon, at 51.2 terabits of switching capacity, is named as the merchant option for clusters that choose Ethernet over InfiniBand.

The Ultra Ethernet Consortium, whose members include AMD, Broadcom, Cisco, Meta, and Microsoft under the Linux Foundation, published a version 1.0 specification in 2025 aimed at making Ethernet match InfiniBand for AI workloads, a direct industry response to NVIDIA's interconnect advantage rather than an independent development, and its member list notably includes companies that are themselves large AI infrastructure builders tracked elsewhere on this site.
